topic_name: How Much Does a Product Grow?
title: One more row adds a whole row
description: Shows that laying one more row along a tray of 23 rows of 27 mangoes adds 27 mangoes, because a product is a rectangle of rows and columns.

title: One more column adds 23
description: Shows 23 × 28 as a 23 by 27 block plus one thin column of 23, so the product grows by 23.

title: Both numbers grow by 1
description: Shows that when 23 and 27 both grow by 1 the rectangle gains a column of 23, a row of 27 and one corner, so the product grows by 51.

title: Bigger and smaller can mean less
description: Compares 5 × 3 with 6 × 2 as dot arrays to show that raising one number by 1 and lowering the other by 1 can make the product smaller.

title: Add one column, add the rows
description: Shows the dot rectangle of the practice tool in its simplest state: 4 rows of 5 dots with one more column of 4 added past a divider, so 4 × 6 = 4 × 5 + 4 × 1.

title: Four parts of 25 × 32
description: Shows 25 × 32 as a rectangle cut into four parts, 23 × 27, 23 × 5, 2 × 27 and 2 × 5, one for each pair of terms.

title: Removed twice, so add 12 back
description: Shows (a − 3)(b − 4) with a = b = 10: removing 4 columns and 3 rows from a 10 by 10 square takes the 3 by 4 corner away twice, so +12 comes back.

title: One term times each of three
description: Shows 3a/2 multiplying each of the three terms a, − b and + 1/5 in turn, giving three unlike terms.

title: Six products, two pairs of like terms
description: Shows the six products of (a + b)(a² + 2ab + b²) and how the two pairs of like terms combine.

title: Four tiles of (5 + z)(y + 9)
description: Shows the binomial tiles in their simplest state: (5 + z)(y + 9) as a rectangle of four tiles, one per pair of terms.

title: Times 11 is the number plus its shift
description: Shows 3874 × 11 as 38740 + 3874, where each column adds a digit and its right hand neighbour.

title: Times 101: shift two places
description: Shows 3874 × 101 as 387400 + 3874, the copy shifted two places, giving 391274.

title: 94 × 11 by adding neighbours
description: Shows 94 × 11 done in one line: the last digit copied, the neighbours 9 and 4 added, then the carry.

title: 65 squared in four pieces
description: Shows the square of side 65 split into a 60 square, a 5 square and two 60 by 5 rectangles, adding to 4225.

title: (a + b)² is more than a² + b²
description: Compares the full square (a + b)² with the two squares a² and b² alone, showing the two missing ab rectangles.

title: The square of 3j + 2k
description: Shows (3j + 2k)² as a square split into 9j², two 6jk rectangles and 4k², with the two 6jk added to 12jk.

title: 104 squared in four tiles
description: Shows the square of sum tiles for 104 = 100 + 4: one big square, two thin strips and a small square.

title: 55 squared from a square of 60
description: Shows 55² as 3600 minus two 60 by 5 strips plus the 5 by 5 corner that was removed twice.

title: (b − 6)² in a sign grid
description: Shows (b − 6)(b − 6) as a 2 by 2 multiplication grid, so both − 6b terms and the + 36 from (−6) × (−6) are seen.

title: Square of a difference in one picture
description: Recaps the square of a difference: from a², take away two a by b strips and add back the b² corner.

topic_name: Patterns and the Difference of Squares
title: Twice 5² + 6² is 11² + 1²
description: Compares two 5 by 5 squares and two 6 by 6 squares with one 11 by 11 square and one 1 by 1 square, both 122.

topic_name: Patterns and the Difference of Squares
title: Move one strip: a² − b² becomes a rectangle
description: Shows that cutting b² from a square of side a and moving one strip makes an (a + b) by (a − b) rectangle.

topic_name: Patterns and the Difference of Squares
title: 197 squared via a round 200
description: Shows 197² worked as (197 + 3)(197 − 3) + 3², with the + 3 that makes 200 highlighted.

topic_name: Patterns and the Difference of Squares
title: From number cases to one identity
description: Shows the identity tool's core move: three number cases of a pattern become one statement with letters, which also passes a test with a negative number and a fraction.

topic_name: Mind the Mistake, Mend the Mistake
title: Mend the forgotten term
description: Shows −3p(−5p + 2q) wrongly simplified to p − 2q, struck out, and the correct 15p² − 6pq from multiplying both terms.

topic_name: Mind the Mistake, Mend the Mistake
title: Unlike terms do not combine
description: Shows that 5w² + 6w cannot be written as 11w², because squares and strips are different kinds of term.

topic_name: Mind the Mistake, Mend the Mistake
title: Sort each product by identity
description: Shows the identity sort in its simplest state: four product cards, each dropped into the bin of the identity that fits.

title: Count the same 15 circles two ways
description: Shows Step 3 of the growing pattern counted two ways, as a 4 by 4 square with one missing and as a 3 by 3 square with two strips of 3, both giving 15 = k² + 2k.

title: A frame of 16 tiles
description: Shows Step 3 of the tile pattern, a 5 by 5 square with a 3 by 3 hole, counted as big square minus hole and as four sides plus corners.

title: One square, two expressions
description: Shows four equal m by n rectangles around a small square, whose area is (m + n)² − 4mn and also (n − m)².

title: Square minus the middle bar
description: Shows the slanted region as an x by x square with a y wide bar down its middle, so its area is x² − xy.

title: Lasso the circles into groups
description: Shows the regrouping tool's core move in its simplest state: Step 2 of the circle pattern lassoed into two groups, giving one expression for the count.

topic_name: Summary: We Distribute, Yet Things Multiply
title: Three ways things multiply
labels: (a + b)(c + d) = ac + ad + bc + bd
description: A clean summary of three results: each term times each term, the square of a sum, and a sum times a difference.

topic_name: Summary: We Distribute, Yet Things Multiply
title: Turn 10 coins upside down in 3 moves
description: Shows that a triangle of 10 coins turns upside down by moving only the three corner coins.
